measurement.name: source-structural-mccabe-v1
measurement.notClaim: Not a full control-flow graph proof or equivalence to every compiler plugin.
measurement.match: Expanded pattern paths minus one; add conservative unmatched exit unless unconditional wildcard/default exists.
measurement.catch: Same path rule when catch cases are present.
measurement.nestedClosures: Include decisions in owning body; report lambda/partial function separately; do not add closure base twice.
measurement.namedNestedDefinitions: Report separately, no nested body counted twice.
measurement.initialization: Report each primary/object initializer and field independently. Abstract declarations have no executable body.
measurement.nesting: Control constructs only; an else-if continuation retains the enclosing if level.

domain.description: Same full forbidden set as the aggregate-rules-formal v3 policy, unchanged; application/infrastructure imports are banned; fixed 5/2 maxima without exceptions.

boundary.appliesTo: app/**/application/** and app/**/infrastructure/** and app/net/** (the shared-common supply)
boundary.description: Projection apply-event contract layer: the generated kernel pure-function classes translate judged events into view rows with zero mechanism, delegating the view's business semantics (empty row / timestamp / text hooks) through constructor-injected per-view semantics faces whose handwritten implementations live in the infrastructure.projection isolation zone; PO unpacking, Await and all IO stay in the glue shell (ViewMachine), which never back-flows into kernel. Per the rulings of 2026-11-19/20 the boundary face admits exactly the declared supply vocabulary (java.time.Instant as the projection time type and java.util.UUID through the net.imadz.common.Id alias — the generated kernel files inline none of them) and Term.Assign is judged by context: named arguments (argument-clause position) are admitted in BOTH layers, assignment targets in neither; kernel isolation and the direction-aware import policy are unchanged.
forbiddenDelta: Term names Instant and UUID are admitted at the boundary as the declared supply face of the handwritten semantics impls and the common Id supply; Random, Clock, LocalDateTime, Date and Await stay banned — clock reads are confined to the two impl files and identity parsing to the common supply by structural properties.

Term.Assign is judged by context, not by layer (E2b ruling): scalameta parses named arguments and assignment targets into the same node, but a named argument always sits in an argument clause (Term.ArgClause parent) while an assignment target never does — named arguments are admitted in BOTH layers, Term.Assign in any other position is a violation in BOTH layers, and Defn.Var stays banned in both layers.

Direction-aware imports: an application file must not import infrastructure packages (kernel isolation); an infrastructure file may import application and infrastructure packages; every other banned import prefix (including java.time/java.util as import statements — fully-qualified type references are the sanctioned zero-import form) stays banned in both directions.
stillRejected: assignment targets (Term.Assign outside an argument clause, in both layers)
mutable collection names and mutation term names
boundary.exceptions: Exact file/owner/kind with finite maxima and justification. No whole-file exemption or project average.

support.description: No forbidden structural checks; 5/2 default with exact closed-dispatch exceptions.
support.exceptions: Exact file/owner/kind with finite maxima and justification.

allow: explicit nominal constructor require for illegal value domain
constructor-injected pure computation (the kernel classes inject their semantics face)
named business-semantic default slots (the untimestamped named default inside the handwritten semantics impls — the family's single sanctioned clock read)
fully-qualified java.time.Instant and net.imadz.common.Id references with zero java.* import statements
named-argument syntax in argument position (the emptyRow/copy emission idiom)
plainFpOo.qualification: Syntactic checks do not alone prove semantic purity or OO responsibility. Exact injected implementation and behavior properties are also reviewed.
